# Single-tablet HIV regimens at Thomas Street Health Center: Stata to R

Teaching material for Hemmige V, Flash CA, Carter J, Giordano TP, Zerai T. Single tablet HIV regimens facilitate virologic suppression and retention in care among treatment naive patients. *AIDS Care.* 2018;30(8):1017-1024. [doi:10.1080/09540121.2018.1442554](https://doi.org/10.1080/09540121.2018.1442554).

The study compared patients starting a single-tablet regimen with those starting three or four pills once a day, using pharmacy fills and laboratory results from a Harris Health System HIV clinic. This repository holds the original Stata code, with patient-level details removed, and a step-by-step translation into R.

The website, which explains every step and shows the R next to the Stata it replaces, is at:
https://vagishhemmige.github.io/Harris-Health-STR/

## Documentation

- [`analysis-plan.md`](analysis-plan.md): what the analysis did, and where the code differs from the paper
- [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md): how the R code is organized
- [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md): how to work in this repository
- [`stata/`](stata/): the original do-files and what was removed from them

## Running the R code

The clinic data are not public and are not here. The R runs on synthetic data:

```r
source("R/synthetic/make_synthetic_data.R")  # writes fake inputs to data-synthetic/
source("R/main.R")                           # runs the translation
```

Packages: dplyr, tidyr, readr, stringr, lubridate, purrr, broom and survey. Results from synthetic data are meaningless and are not results of the study.
